name: FLS 1 field (Hubble)
blurb: A deep field toward the dusty starburst galaxy FLS 1, seen by Hubble.
label: fls1-hubble
story: Somewhere in this field lies FLS 1, a dusty galaxy forming stars furiously in the early universe, found by the Herschel observatory. Hubble looked here to measure its size and stars, to check whether a foreground galaxy magnifies it, and to see whether it belongs to a gathering protocluster.

claims.text: RARE-FLS-1 is the dusty starburst FLS107 / 1HERMES-S250-J170817.6+582845, one of the brightest spectroscopically confirmed dusty starbursts at z=4.2 to 5.3, selected from Herschel-HerMES
The source is called FLS 1 in the Herschel/SPIRE discovery paper, at the field position, with a CO redshift of 4.29
Hubble aimed to measure sizes and stellar masses, test for gravitational lensing, and check protocluster membership
These are among the earliest dusty starbursts (early universe)
